1	# Creating a command
2	
3	Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).
4	
5	Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:
10	
11	```js
12	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
13	import { z } from 'zod';
14	import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';
15	
16	export const blendArg = defineArgument({
17	  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
18	  description: 'Blend of coffee',
19	  placeholder: 'blend',
20	});
21	```
22	
23	`--shots`, `--milk` and `--topping` are only used by this subcommand, so they are defined inline. `--format` comes from `global.options.js`:
24

28	import { brewCoffee } from '../../clever-client/coffee.js';
29	import { defineCommand } from '../../lib/define-command.js';

31	import { Logger } from '../../logger.js';

33	import { humanJsonOutputFormatOption } from '../global.options.js';
34	import { blendArg } from './coffee.args.js';
35

46	    }),

1	# Clever Cloud API client
2	
3	clever-tools talks to the Clever Cloud API through [`clever-client.js`](https://github.com/CleverCloud/clever-client.js), published as `@clevercloud/client` and pinned in `package.json`.
4	
5	## The pattern used in `src/`
6	
7	Every command and model uses the function-per-endpoint API of the client, combined with `sendToApi` from `src/models/send-to-api.js`:
8	
9	```js
10	import { updateEnvVar } from '@clevercloud/client/esm/api/v2/application.js';
11	import { sendToApi } from '../../models/send-to-api.js';
12	
13	await updateEnvVar({ id: ownerId, appId, envName }, { value }).then(sendToApi);
14	```
15	
16	The endpoint function only builds the request params (method, URL, headers, body). `sendToApi` then:
17	
18	- prefixes the URL with `API_HOST` (overridable per profile or with an env var),
19	- signs the request with the OAuth tokens of the active profile,
20	- logs the method and URL at debug level (`-v`),
21	- turns network, TLS and 401 errors into messages the user can act on (`processError`).
22	
23	Other API errors are rethrown as is, so their message depends on the endpoint. Run with `-v` to see the request.
24	
25	Related helpers in the same file:
26	
27	- `sendToAuthBridge`: same pipeline against `AUTH_BRIDGE_HOST` (API tokens, see `src/commands/tokens/`).
28	- `sendToApiWithConfig`: same pipeline with explicit credentials, for a profile that is not the active one (`src/lib/profile.js`, login).
29	- `getHostAndTokens`: host and tokens for the streaming helpers (`@clevercloud/client/esm/streams/*`: logs and access logs, and `activity --follow` through a WebSocket).
30	
31	## Resolving IDs
32	
33	Commands accept names or IDs (`--app`, `--alias`, `--org`, add-on names…). Never resolve them by hand in a command:
34	
35	- `Application.resolveId(appIdOrName, alias)` (`src/models/application.js`) returns `{ ownerId, appId }`, falling back to the app linked in `.clever.json`.
36	- `src/models/ids-resolver.js` resolves owners, add-ons and OAuth consumers, with a local cache (`src/config/cache.js`, `IDS_CACHE_FILE`).
37	- Operators, k8s and network groups resolve names in their own models and throw the error built by `ambiguousNameError()` (`src/lib/ambiguous-name-error.js`) when a name matches several resources.
38	
39	## Endpoints missing from the client
40	
41	`src/clever-client/` holds endpoints that `@clevercloud/client` does not expose (auth bridge, drains, k8s, network groups, operators). The request-params part of `@clevercloud/client` is no longer updated, so adding an endpoint here is the normal way to get a missing one, no issue or PR on `clever-client.js` is needed.
42	
43	Before adding one, check that the endpoint does not already exist in `@clevercloud/client` (`node_modules/@clevercloud/client/dist/esm/api/`).
44

**What I found**
- Kubernetes quotas are per organisation, not per cluster. The endpoint is `GET /v4/kubernetes/organisations/{ownerId}/quota`.
- That endpoint (`getK8sQuota` in `src/clever-client/k8s.js`) and a helper (`k8sGetQuota(orgIdOrName)` in `src/lib/k8s.js`) already exist, but no command uses them yet.
- So the command takes `--org` and `--format` and no cluster argument, like `k8s list`.
- The helper's JSDoc describes the payload as `{ id, tenantId, tags, quotas }`. I don't know the exact shape of `quotas`.
- Dependencies aren't installed here (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`), so I couldn't run the CLI or call the API.

**What I'd add once you allow edits**
- `k8s.quota.command.js`, modelled on `k8s.list`/`k8s.get`, with `since: null`. It has `--org` and `--format`. JSON output prints the raw payload. Human output prints a `console.table` of `quotas`, plus a message when there are none.
- A registration in `global.commands.js`: the import, and `quota: k8sQuotaCommand` in the `k8s` subcommands.
- After that, `npm install`, `npm run docs` and `npm run validate`. I'd also run it against a test account to check the real `quotas` shape and adjust the human output.
